questions.question: What does an eight-sided (octagonal) red and white sign mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Stop completely
questions.explanation: An octagonal sign is always a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, even if no other traffic is present.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: eight sides means STOP - count the sides like T-Rexy counts his tiny arms!

questions.question: What shape and color is a yield sign?
questions.correctAnswer: An upside-down triangle, red and white
questions.explanation: Yield signs are upside-down (inverted) triangles in red and white. They tell you to slow down and give the right-of-way to other traffic.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a yield sign points DOWN - yield to whoever is already there!

questions.question: A white rectangular sign with black numbers showing 45 means:
questions.correctAnswer: The maximum legal speed is 45 mph
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs show the maximum speed allowed under ideal conditions. You may drive slower, but never faster.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the number on the sign is the CEILING, not the floor - never go above it!

questions.question: What should you do when you see a DO NOT ENTER sign?
questions.correctAnswer: Do not drive onto that road or ramp
questions.explanation: DO NOT ENTER means the road is for one-way traffic in the opposite direction. Entering could cause a head-on crash.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: do not enter means DO NOT ENTER - your car is not a salmon swimming upstream!

questions.question: A ONE WAY sign tells you:
questions.correctAnswer: Traffic on this street moves in only one direction
distractors: You may only make one turn here
Only one car may pass at a time
questions.explanation: ONE WAY signs mark streets where all traffic flows in a single direction. Check for them before turning onto an unfamiliar street.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: one way means one way - going the wrong way makes you the villain in an action movie!

questions.question: What does a NO U-TURN sign mean?
questions.correctAnswer: You may not make a U-turn at this location
distractors: You may turn around only at night
Trucks may not turn around here
questions.explanation: A NO U-TURN sign prohibits reversing your direction at that spot, usually because visibility is limited or traffic is heavy.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the U-turn arrow has a big red NO - respect the NO!

questions.question: A NO PARKING sign means you:
questions.correctAnswer: May stop briefly to load passengers but may not leave your car
distractors: May park for up to 5 minutes
Must never stop here at all
questions.explanation: NO PARKING means you cannot leave your vehicle unattended, though you may stop momentarily to pick up or drop off passengers.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: no parking means no naps for your car - keep it moving!

questions.question: If you see a WRONG WAY sign, you should:
questions.correctAnswer: Turn around immediately and safely as soon as possible
distractors: Flash your headlights and keep going
questions.explanation: A WRONG WAY sign means you are driving against traffic. Get off the road safely at once - you are in extreme danger of a head-on collision.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: wrong way is VERY wrong - turn around like you forgot your phone at home!

questions.question: A divided highway sign (two roadways separated) warns you that:
questions.correctAnswer: The road splits into two one-way roadways with a median between them
questions.explanation: Divided highway signs alert you that opposing traffic is separated by a median. Keep right and never cross the median except at designated openings.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: divided means split - stay on YOUR side of the split!

questions.question: What does a NO TURN ON RED sign mean?
questions.correctAnswer: You must wait for a green light before turning, even after stopping
distractors: You may turn after stopping twice
Only trucks must wait for green
You may turn on red after 10 seconds
questions.explanation: Normally you may turn right on red after a complete stop. This sign removes that option at this intersection - no turning at all until the light turns green.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: no turn on red means your turn waits - patience, driver!

questions.question: A KEEP RIGHT sign tells drivers to:
questions.correctAnswer: Stay to the right of a divider, island, or obstruction
distractors: Drive only in the right lane
questions.explanation: KEEP RIGHT signs are placed at traffic islands and dividers. Pass on the right side of the obstruction.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: keep right - the sign is literally pointing you right!

questions.question: What does a DO NOT PASS sign indicate?
questions.correctAnswer: Passing other vehicles is prohibited in this zone
distractors: Trucks may not use this lane
questions.explanation: DO NOT PASS marks zones where passing is unsafe, such as near hills, curves, or intersections with limited visibility.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: do not pass - your patience is a superpower here!

questions.question: A railroad crossbuck (the X-shaped sign at tracks) means:
questions.correctAnswer: Yield to trains - a train may be approaching
questions.explanation: The crossbuck is the basic railroad crossing sign. Treat it like a yield sign: look, listen, and give trains the right-of-way.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the X marks the tracks - trains ALWAYS win a tie!

questions.question: A STOP HERE ON RED sign with a white stop line tells you:
questions.correctAnswer: Stop your vehicle before the white line, not in the crosswalk
distractors: Stop only if pedestrians are present
questions.explanation: You must stop before the stop line so you do not block the crosswalk or intersection. The line marks the legal stopping point.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: stop BEFORE the line - the line is the boss!

questions.question: A diamond-shaped marking painted on a lane (and matching signs) designates:
questions.correctAnswer: An HOV (carpool) lane for vehicles with 2 or more occupants
distractors: A lane for emergency vehicles only
questions.explanation: In Arizona, diamond symbols mark HOV lanes, generally for vehicles carrying two or more people during posted hours.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: diamonds are a carpooler's best friend - bring a buddy!

questions.question: Diamond-shaped yellow signs are:
questions.correctAnswer: Warning signs that alert you to hazards ahead
questions.explanation: Yellow diamond signs warn of upcoming hazards like curves, intersections, or road conditions. Slow down and stay alert.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: yellow diamonds WARN you - like a caution flag at the races!

questions.question: What shape is a school zone warning sign?
questions.correctAnswer: A five-sided pentagon
questions.explanation: School advance-warning signs are pentagons (five sides). When you see one, slow down and watch for children.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: five sides for school - count them on your way past!

questions.question: A yellow diamond sign showing a walking person means:
questions.correctAnswer: A pedestrian crossing is ahead - watch for people on foot
distractors: Jogging is allowed on this road
questions.explanation: Pedestrian crossing signs warn that people may be crossing. Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: walking person sign means real walking people - brake for feet!

questions.question: A round yellow sign with a black X and the letter R means:
questions.correctAnswer: A railroad crossing is ahead
questions.explanation: The round yellow advance sign warns of a railroad crossing ahead. Prepare to stop if a train is coming.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: round yellow X means choo-choo is near - ears open!

questions.question: A MERGE sign (two lanes becoming one) tells you to:
questions.correctAnswer: Adjust speed and blend smoothly with traffic in the continuing lane
questions.explanation: Merging requires matching the speed of traffic and finding a safe gap. Drivers in the through lane should make room when possible.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: merging is like joining a dance - match the rhythm, don't step on toes!

questions.question: A SLIPPERY WHEN WET sign warns that:
questions.correctAnswer: The road surface becomes dangerously slick in rain
distractors: Only wet tires may use the road
questions.explanation: Oil and dust make Arizona roads especially slick during the first minutes of rain. Slow down and increase following distance.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: wet roads are slippery - Arizona rain plus oil equals ice-like slick!

questions.question: A yellow diamond sign with a leaping deer means:
questions.correctAnswer: Wildlife may cross the road here
questions.explanation: Animal crossing signs mark areas where wildlife frequently crosses. Scan the roadside, especially at dawn and dusk.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: leaping deer sign means Bambi might dash out - eyes up!

questions.question: What does a sharp turn (hairpin curve) warning sign tell you?
questions.correctAnswer: Slow down significantly - a very sharp curve is ahead
questions.explanation: Hairpin curve signs warn of an extremely sharp bend. Reduce speed well before the curve, not during it.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: hairpin ahead - slow down BEFORE the curve, not in it!

questions.question: A DIVIDED HIGHWAY ENDS sign means:
questions.correctAnswer: The median is ending and two-way traffic will be undivided ahead
questions.explanation: When the divided highway ends, opposing traffic will be directly beside you with no median. Stay alert and centered in your lane.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the median is ending - oncoming traffic is about to get closer!

questions.question: A LOW CLEARANCE sign (such as 12' 6") warns:
questions.correctAnswer: Tall vehicles that the overhead clearance is limited
questions.explanation: Low clearance signs matter most for trucks, RVs, and vehicles with roof loads. Know your vehicle's height.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: know your height - bridges don't move for tall trucks!

questions.question: A yellow diamond sign showing a bicycle means:
questions.correctAnswer: A bicycle crossing or bike lane is ahead - share the road
questions.explanation: Bicycle warning signs remind drivers that cyclists may be present. Give them space and pass with at least 3 feet of clearance in Arizona.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: bike sign means share the road - cyclists are traffic too!

questions.question: Orange diamond signs indicate:
questions.correctAnswer: Construction or work zones with possible lane changes and workers
questions.explanation: Orange is the color of construction zones. Slow down, follow flagger directions, and expect fines to double for violations.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: orange means construction - slow down, workers are someone's family!

questions.question: A steady red traffic light means:
questions.correctAnswer: Stop completely and wait for green
questions.explanation: A steady red light requires a full stop. Remain stopped until the light turns green, unless a sign says otherwise.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: red means STOP, full stop - no rolling!

questions.question: When may you turn right on a steady red light in Arizona?
questions.correctAnswer: After coming to a complete stop and yielding, unless a sign prohibits it
distractors: Without stopping if no cars are coming
questions.explanation: Right turn on red is legal in Arizona after a full stop and yielding to traffic and pedestrians, unless a NO TURN ON RED sign is posted.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: red light right turn: stop first, look, then go - like a stop sign!

questions.question: A steady yellow traffic light means:
questions.correctAnswer: The light is about to turn red - stop if you can do so safely
distractors: Speed up to beat the red
questions.explanation: Yellow warns the signal is changing to red. Stop if you can safely; if you are too close to stop safely, proceed through carefully.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: yellow means prepare to stop - not floor it!

questions.question: A flashing red traffic light means:
questions.correctAnswer: Stop completely, then proceed when safe - like a stop sign
distractors: Slow down but do not stop
The signal is broken - ignore it
questions.explanation: Treat a flashing red light exactly like a stop sign: stop fully, yield to traffic with the right-of-way, then go.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: flashing red is a stop sign in disguise!

questions.question: A flashing yellow traffic light means:
questions.correctAnswer: Proceed with caution - you have the right-of-way but stay alert
questions.explanation: Flashing yellow means proceed carefully without stopping, but watch for cross traffic that may have a flashing red or stop sign.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: flashing yellow means cruise with caution - eyes wide open!

questions.question: If you face a green arrow together with a red light, you may:
questions.correctAnswer: Turn in the direction of the arrow without stopping
distractors: Stop and wait for full green
questions.explanation: A green arrow gives you a protected turn in the arrow's direction. Other movements must still wait for green.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: green arrow is your VIP pass - turn that way, no stop needed!

questions.question: At a four-way stop, who goes first?
questions.correctAnswer: The vehicle that arrived first
questions.explanation: Arrival order decides it - whoever completes their stop first goes first. If you cannot tell who was first, wave the other driver through: courtesy prevents the both-go-at-once crash.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: first come, first served - four-way stops are polite democracy!

questions.question: At a four-way stop, if two vehicles arrive at the same time, who yields?
questions.correctAnswer: The driver on the left yields to the driver on the right
distractors: Both go at the same time
The driver going straight always goes first
questions.explanation: When arrival is simultaneous, yield to the vehicle on your right. When in doubt, let the other driver go first.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: tie at a four-way? Yield to the RIGHT - right is right!

questions.question: When entering a roundabout, you must:
questions.correctAnswer: Yield to traffic already circulating in the roundabout
questions.explanation: Roundabouts flow counterclockwise. Yield to vehicles already in the circle, enter to the right, and exit from the right lane.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: roundabout rule: those INSIDE own the circle - yield to them!

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection, you must yield to:
questions.correctAnswer: Oncoming traffic and pedestrians
distractors: No one - left turns have priority
questions.explanation: Left turns cross the path of oncoming traffic. Yield until the way is clear, and watch for pedestrians in the crosswalk.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: left turners wait - oncoming traffic goes first!

questions.question: Who has the right-of-way at a crosswalk?
questions.correctAnswer: Pedestrians - drivers must yield whether the crosswalk is marked or not
distractors: Drivers, unless the light is red
questions.explanation: In Arizona, drivers must yield to pedestrians in any crosswalk, marked or unmarked. Every intersection is legally a crosswalk.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: feet beat wheels at crosswalks - pedestrians always win!

questions.question: When entering a road from a driveway, alley, or parking lot, you must:
questions.correctAnswer: Yield to traffic and pedestrians already on the road or sidewalk
questions.explanation: Vehicles entering from driveways or alleys must yield to everyone already on the roadway, including people on the sidewalk.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: driveways are the minor leagues - the main road has priority!

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights and siren approaches, you should:
questions.correctAnswer: Pull to the right edge of the road and stop until it passes
distractors: Speed up to stay ahead of it
questions.explanation: Move right and stop to let emergency vehicles pass. Never follow within 500 feet of a responding fire truck.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: lights and sirens mean MOVE RIGHT - lives depend on it!

questions.question: At an intersection with no signs or signals, who yields?
questions.correctAnswer: Yield to the vehicle on your right
distractors: The vehicle going straight always stops
questions.explanation: At uncontrolled intersections, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right. Slow down and be prepared to stop.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: no signs? Look RIGHT - yield to whoever is there!

questions.question: You must not cut through or disrupt:
questions.correctAnswer: A funeral procession
questions.explanation: It is illegal and disrespectful to cut into or through a funeral procession. Yield to processions and do not separate the vehicles.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: funeral processions get respect - never cut through!

questions.question: Unless otherwise posted, the speed limit in Arizona residential and business districts is:
questions.correctAnswer: 25 mph
questions.explanation: Arizona's default speed limit is 25 mph in residential and business districts. Always watch for posted signs that may differ.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: 25 in neighborhoods - kids and pets live there!

questions.question: The speed limit in a school zone in Arizona is:
questions.correctAnswer: 15 mph
questions.explanation: School zones are 15 mph in Arizona when children are present or when lights are flashing. Slow down and watch carefully.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: 15 near schools - children are unpredictable, your speed shouldn't be!

questions.question: Unless otherwise posted, the maximum speed limit on a rural interstate highway in Arizona is:
questions.correctAnswer: 75 mph
questions.explanation: Arizona law sets the maximum speed on interstate highways in rural areas at 75 mph unless a lower limit is posted. On other Arizona highways, the statutory maximum is 65 mph.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: rural interstates fly at 75 - other highways top out at 65, and posted signs always win!

questions.question: When roads are wet or dusty, you should:
questions.correctAnswer: Reduce your speed below the posted limit
distractors: Drive the posted limit no matter what
Speed up to get through quickly
questions.explanation: Posted limits are for ideal conditions. Slow down in rain, dust, or low visibility - the basic speed law requires a safe speed for conditions.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: bad weather means slow down - the sign's number is for sunny days!

questions.question: In an HOV (carpool) lane, the speed limit is:
questions.correctAnswer: The same as the posted speed limit for the highway
distractors: There is no speed limit in HOV lanes
questions.explanation: The diamond changes WHO may use the lane, not how fast anyone may drive. The speed limit sign sets the limit for the HOV lane too - carpooling buys you a clearer lane, not a higher limit.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: HOV saves time, not speed limits - same rules apply!

questions.question: When must you obey a 15 mph school zone speed limit?
questions.correctAnswer: When children are present or warning lights are flashing
distractors: Only on school days at 8 AM
At all times, day and night
Only when a crossing guard is visible
questions.explanation: The 15 mph limit is not in force 24/7 - it switches on when children are coming or going, which is exactly what the flashing beacons announce. Outside those times the regular posted limit applies, but stay alert near schools anyway.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: kids present or lights flashing means 15 - no excuses!

questions.question: Fines for speeding in a work (construction) zone are:
questions.correctAnswer: Doubled
questions.explanation: A violation that costs $100 elsewhere costs $200 in a work zone - Arizona doubles fines to protect workers standing feet from live traffic, and the doubling applies even when you cannot see a crew at that moment.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: work zone fines DOUBLE - slow down, it is cheaper and safer!

questions.question: Arizona's basic speed law requires you to:
questions.correctAnswer: Never drive faster than is safe for current conditions
questions.explanation: Even at or below the posted limit, you can be cited for driving too fast for conditions like rain, dust, or heavy traffic.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the basic speed law: safe beats legal - conditions rule!

questions.question: When parallel parking, your wheels must be within what distance of the curb?
questions.correctAnswer: 18 inches
questions.explanation: Arizona law (A.R.S. 28-874) requires your wheels to be within 18 inches of the curb when you parallel park. If the gap is wider than 18 inches, your car sticks too far into the traffic lane and you can be cited.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: 18 inches from the curb, max - about a ruler and a half!

questions.question: You may not park within what distance of a fire hydrant?
questions.correctAnswer: 15 feet
questions.explanation: Keep 15 feet clear of fire hydrants so firefighters can connect hoses in an emergency.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: 15 feet from hydrants - firefighters need room to save lives!

questions.question: You may not park within what distance of a crosswalk?
questions.correctAnswer: 20 feet
questions.explanation: Parking too close to a crosswalk blocks drivers' view of pedestrians. Arizona requires 20 feet of clearance.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: 20 feet from crosswalks - don't block the view of walkers!

questions.question: You may not park within what distance of a stop sign or traffic signal?
questions.correctAnswer: 30 feet
questions.explanation: Arizona prohibits parking within 30 feet of a stop sign, yield sign, or traffic signal so they remain visible.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: 30 feet from signs and signals - keep them visible!

questions.question: Is it legal to park in front of a private driveway?
questions.correctAnswer: No - never block a driveway
distractors: Yes, if your hazards are on
questions.explanation: Blocking a driveway is illegal at all times. Driveways must remain clear for vehicles entering and exiting.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: driveways are exits, not parking spots - never block them!

questions.question: Who may park in a space marked with the wheelchair symbol?
questions.correctAnswer: Only vehicles displaying a valid disabled placard or plate
questions.explanation: Disabled parking spaces are reserved for people with disabilities displaying proper placards or plates. Violations carry heavy fines.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: blue wheelchair spaces are reserved - need the placard to park there!

questions.question: When parking downhill next to a curb, turn your front wheels:
questions.correctAnswer: Toward the curb
questions.explanation: Turning wheels toward the curb downhill means if the brakes fail, the car rolls into the curb instead of traffic.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: downhill: wheels TO the curb - let the curb catch you!

questions.question: When parking uphill next to a curb, turn your front wheels:
questions.correctAnswer: Away from the curb
questions.explanation: Uphill with a curb, turn wheels away so the back of the tire catches the curb if the car rolls backward.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: uphill: wheels AWAY from curb - the curb is your safety net!

questions.question: In Arizona, it is illegal for a driver age 21 or older to drive with a BAC of:
questions.correctAnswer: 0.08% or higher
questions.explanation: 'Per se' means the number itself is the crime: at 0.08% the state does not have to prove you felt drunk. And you can still be charged below 0.08 if an officer observes impairment - many drivers are dangerous well under the line.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: 0.08 is the line - cross it and you are DUI!

questions.question: For drivers under age 21, Arizona's BAC limit is:
questions.correctAnswer: 0.00% - zero tolerance
questions.explanation: Arizona has zero tolerance for underage drinking and driving. Any measurable alcohol can lead to DUI charges.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: under 21 means ZERO alcohol - not a drop!

questions.question: Under Arizona's implied consent law, refusing a chemical BAC test after a DUI arrest results in:
questions.correctAnswer: Automatic 12-month driver license suspension
questions.explanation: By driving in Arizona you have already consented to testing. A first refusal brings an automatic 12-month license suspension.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: refuse the test, lose the license for a YEAR - implied consent!

questions.question: In Arizona, an Extreme DUI is charged at a BAC of:
questions.correctAnswer: 0.15% or higher
questions.explanation: Extreme DUI (0.15%+) carries a mandatory minimum 30 days in jail on a first offense, much harsher than standard DUI.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: 0.15 is EXTREME - 30 days in jail minimum!

questions.question: A Super Extreme DUI in Arizona applies at a BAC of:
questions.correctAnswer: 0.20% or higher
questions.explanation: Super Extreme DUI (0.20%+) is Arizona's highest misdemeanor DUI tier, with at least 45 days jail on a first offense.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: 0.20 is SUPER extreme - the penalties are super-sized too!

questions.question: A first standard DUI conviction in Arizona results in a license suspension of:
questions.correctAnswer: 90 days
questions.explanation: A first DUI brings a 90-day MVD suspension: 30 days of no driving, then 60 days restricted driving.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: first DUI means 90 days of license trouble - 30 with zero driving!

questions.question: What is the ONLY thing that can sober you up after drinking?
questions.correctAnswer: Time
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your system - about one hour per standard drink. Coffee and cold air just make a wide-awake drunk driver.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: only TIME sobers you up - coffee just makes you a jittery drunk driver!

questions.question: In Arizona, having an open container of alcohol in a vehicle is:
questions.correctAnswer: Illegal for both drivers and passengers
distractors: Legal if the driver is sober
questions.explanation: Arizona prohibits open containers of alcohol in the passenger area for everyone in the vehicle, driver and passengers alike.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: open containers are a NO for everyone in the car!

questions.question: Can prescription or over-the-counter drugs lead to a DUI?
questions.correctAnswer: Yes - any drug that impairs driving can lead to DUI
questions.explanation: Arizona DUI law covers impairment by any drug, including legal prescriptions and over-the-counter medicines. Read labels for driving warnings.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: legal pills can still mean illegal driving - check the label!

questions.question: The safest choice if you plan to drink alcohol is to:
questions.correctAnswer: Arrange a designated sober driver or alternate ride in advance
questions.explanation: Plan ahead: a sober driver, rideshare, or taxi. There is no safe way to drive after drinking.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: plan the ride BEFORE the drink - designated drivers are heroes!

questions.question: After most first-offense DUI convictions in Arizona, drivers must install:
questions.correctAnswer: An ignition interlock device for 12 months
questions.explanation: Arizona requires an ignition interlock device (a breath-test starter lock) for 12 months after most first DUI convictions.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: DUI means blowing into a tube to start your car for a YEAR!

questions.question: The BAC limit for commercial vehicle drivers in Arizona is:
questions.explanation: Commercial drivers face a stricter 0.04% limit because of the size and danger of their vehicles.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: big rig, small limit - 0.04 for commercial drivers!

questions.question: In Arizona, who is legally required to wear a seat belt in the front seat?
questions.correctAnswer: Every front-seat occupant
questions.explanation: Arizona law requires all front-seat occupants, driver and passengers, to be buckled while the vehicle is moving.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: front seat means buckle up - EVERYONE up front!

questions.question: Arizona's seat belt law for adults is secondary enforcement, which means:
questions.correctAnswer: An officer cannot stop you for a seat belt violation alone
questions.explanation: For adults, officers may only cite a seat belt violation after stopping you for another offense. The fine is a maximum of $10.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: secondary means they need ANOTHER reason to stop you first!

questions.question: Passengers under age 16 in Arizona must wear seat belts:
questions.correctAnswer: In every seating position, front and back
questions.explanation: Arizona requires every passenger under 16 to be buckled in all seats. Adults 16+ in the back seat are not legally required, though it is far safer.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: under 16 means buckled EVERYWHERE in the car!

questions.question: In Arizona, a child under age 5 must ride in:
questions.correctAnswer: A federally approved child restraint system
distractors: Any seat with a seat belt
questions.explanation: Children under 5 must be in a proper child restraint (car seat or booster meeting federal standards).
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: under 5 means a real car seat - laps are not restraints!

questions.question: Arizona requires a booster seat until a child is:
questions.correctAnswer: 8 years old or 4 feet 9 inches tall, whichever comes first
questions.explanation: Children ages 5 through 7 who are 4'9" or shorter must use a child restraint, usually a booster. At 8 or over 4'9", a seat belt is legally permitted.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: booster until 8 or 4 foot 9 - whichever comes FIRST!

questions.question: Violating Arizona's child restraint law carries:
questions.correctAnswer: A $50 civil penalty, and officers can stop you for it alone (primary enforcement)
questions.explanation: Unlike adult seat belt violations, child restraint violations are primary enforcement with a $50 penalty - officers can stop you just for this.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: kids unbuckled means a $50 ticket AND they can pull you over for it!

questions.question: When passing a bicyclist in Arizona, you must leave at least:
questions.correctAnswer: 3 feet of space
questions.explanation: Arizona requires at least 3 feet of clearance when passing a bicycle. Slow down and pass only when safe.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: 3 feet for bikes - give cyclists their bubble!

questions.question: When sharing a lane with a motorcycle, you should:
questions.correctAnswer: Give the motorcycle the full lane - never share or crowd it
distractors: Share the lane side by side
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are entitled to a full lane. Never try to share a lane with one, and check blind spots carefully - bikes are hard to see.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: motorcycles get the WHOLE lane - they are not half-vehicles!

questions.question: When a school bus stops with red lights flashing, you must:
questions.correctAnswer: Stop in both directions
distractors: Stop only if behind the bus
questions.explanation: Stop for school buses with flashing red lights from both directions to protect loading children.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: red flashing bus lights mean STOP - kids are crossing!

questions.question: You do NOT need to stop for a school bus with flashing red lights when:
questions.correctAnswer: You are on the opposite side of a divided highway with a physical barrier
questions.explanation: On a divided roadway with a median or barrier, oncoming traffic need not stop. Otherwise, both directions must stop.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: divided highway with a barrier is the ONLY exception to bus stopping!

questions.question: Arizona's Move Over law requires you to:
questions.correctAnswer: Move over one lane or slow down for stopped emergency and work vehicles
questions.explanation: When approaching stopped emergency, tow, or highway work vehicles with flashing lights, move over a lane or reduce speed if you cannot.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: move OVER or slow DOWN - protect those who protect you!

questions.question: When you see a pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, you must:
questions.correctAnswer: Always yield the right-of-way
questions.explanation: Pedestrians who are blind or visually impaired always have the right-of-way. Stop and let them cross completely.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: white cane means STOP - always yield, no exceptions!

questions.question: When driving near livestock or horses on the road, you should:
questions.correctAnswer: Slow down and never honk or rev your engine
questions.explanation: Animals spook easily. Slow down, give them space, and avoid loud noises that could cause them to bolt into traffic.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: horses spook at honks - quiet and slow wins!

questions.question: Large trucks have:
questions.correctAnswer: Much larger blind spots than cars
questions.explanation: Truck blind spots (no-zones) are huge - directly in front, behind, and along both sides. If you can't see the driver's mirrors, they can't see you.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: if you can't see their mirrors, they can't see YOU!

questions.question: You should avoid cutting in front of a large truck because:
questions.correctAnswer: Trucks need much longer distances to stop
questions.explanation: A loaded truck at highway speed can need nearly twice the stopping distance of a car. Cutting in removes their safety cushion.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: trucks can't stop on a dime - don't steal their braking room!

questions.question: When a truck is turning right, you should:
questions.correctAnswer: Stay back - trucks swing wide and may need both lanes
questions.explanation: Trucks make wide right turns and may swing left first. Never try to pass a turning truck on the right.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: wide turns need wide space - never squeeze by a turning truck!

questions.question: In good conditions, you should keep a following distance of:
questions.correctAnswer: 3 to 4 seconds behind the vehicle ahead
distractors: One car length per 10 mph only
questions.explanation: A 3-4 second gap gives you time to react. Increase it in rain, dust, or when following trucks or motorcycles.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: 3 to 4 seconds of space - count it out: one-thousand-one...

questions.question: Arizona requires headlights to be on:
questions.correctAnswer: From sunset to sunrise
questions.explanation: Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise, and any time visibility is poor. They help others see you, not just you see.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: sunset to sunrise means LIGHTS ON - be seen!

questions.question: You must dim your high beams when an oncoming vehicle is within:
questions.correctAnswer: 500 feet
questions.explanation: Dim to low beams within 500 feet of oncoming traffic (and 300 feet when following) so you don't blind other drivers.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: 500 feet means dim - don't blind oncoming drivers!

questions.question: If blinded by oncoming headlights at night, you should:
questions.correctAnswer: Look toward the right edge of your lane until the vehicle passes
questions.explanation: Glance at the right edge line to keep your lane position while the bright vehicle passes. Never stare into high beams.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: blinded? Look RIGHT at the edge line - not at the lights!

questions.question: If your car starts to hydroplane on wet pavement, you should:
questions.correctAnswer: Ease off the gas and steer straight without hard braking
distractors: Shift to neutral and close your eyes
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning means your tires are riding on water. Ease off the accelerator, keep the wheel straight, and avoid sudden moves until grip returns.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: hydroplaning? Easy off the gas, straight wheel, NO panic braking!

questions.question: If your brakes fail while driving, you should:
questions.correctAnswer: Pump the brakes, downshift, and use the parking brake gradually
distractors: Open the door and jump out
questions.explanation: Pump the brake pedal to build pressure, shift to a lower gear, and apply the parking brake slowly. Steer to a safe area.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: brakes fail? Pump, downshift, parking brake - in that order!

questions.question: If a tire blows out at speed, you should:
questions.correctAnswer: Grip the wheel firmly, ease off the gas, and slow gradually
questions.explanation: A blowout pulls the car toward the flat tire. Hold the wheel steady, ease off the gas, and brake gently once slowed.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: blowout? Grip tight, ease off gas - no sudden moves!

questions.question: If your vehicle stalls on railroad tracks, you should:
questions.correctAnswer: Get everyone out immediately and move away from the tracks
distractors: Try to restart the engine for 5 minutes
questions.explanation: If a train is coming, abandon the vehicle at once and move away at a 45-degree angle from the tracks. Your life matters more than the car.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: stalled on tracks? GET OUT - cars are replaceable, you are not!

questions.question: If caught in an Arizona dust storm while driving, you should:
questions.correctAnswer: Pull completely off the roadway, turn off all lights, take your foot off the brake, and wait
distractors: Turn on hazards and keep driving slowly
Speed up to get through it
questions.explanation: ADOT's 'Pull Aside, Stay Alive' rule: get fully off the pavement, kill all lights (others follow taillights into crashes), foot off the brake, stay buckled.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: dust storm? Pull ASIDE, stay ALIVE - off road, lights OFF!

questions.question: During a dust storm, why must you turn OFF your lights after pulling over?
questions.correctAnswer: Other drivers may follow your lights and crash into you
distractors: It is the law to save fuel
questions.explanation: In near-zero visibility, drivers instinctively follow lights. A glowing stopped car becomes a target for rear-end collisions.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: lights OFF in dust - glowing cars get rear-ended!

questions.question: Arizona's 'Stupid Motorist Law' means:
questions.correctAnswer: Drivers who go around barricades into flooded areas can be charged for rescue costs
questions.explanation: Under A.R.S. 28-910, motorists who drive around barricades into flooded roadways may be billed for their rescue. Turn around, don't drown.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: barricades mean TURN AROUND - or pay for your own rescue!

questions.question: Arizona's hands-free driving law prohibits:
questions.correctAnswer: Holding a phone in your hand while driving
questions.explanation: Since 2019, Arizona drivers may not hold or support a phone with their body while driving. Use hands-free or pull over.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: phone in hand means ticket in hand - go hands-free!

questions.question: To legally use an HOV (carpool) lane in the Phoenix area, your vehicle must have:
questions.correctAnswer: At least 2 occupants
questions.explanation: Arizona HOV lanes generally require 2 or more occupants during posted hours. Motorcycles and buses may also qualify.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: HOV means 2 or more - solo drivers stay out!

questions.question: Arizona's monsoon season, bringing dust storms and flash floods, runs from:
questions.correctAnswer: Mid-June through September
questions.explanation: The monsoon officially runs June 15 through September 30. Expect sudden dust storms, heavy rain, and flash flooding in washes.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: monsoon is June to September - expect dust and flash floods!
